findings.title: Missing re-check of cache after acquiring write lock causes redundant recomputation under concurrent first-time load
findings.body:
After taking the write lock at line 48, the function does not re-check whether another goroutine has populated `entryPointAssetsCache` while this goroutine was waiting for the lock. In non-Dev mode with an initially empty cache, multiple concurrent first-time callers will all see `nil` under the read lock, enter the write path, serialize on the write lock, and each independently re-read and re-parse the manifest and overwrite the cache. The consequence is wasted I/O and CPU at startup. Add a second check under the write lock so only the first caller does the work:

entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()
defer entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Unlock()
if entryPointAssetsCache != nil && cfg.Env != setting.Dev {
    return entryPointAssetsCache, nil
}

Additionally, the write path unconditionally overwrites the cache with `result` even when `readWebAssetsFromFile` returns an error (result == nil, err != nil). This pre-existing cache-poisoning bug is now reachable from concurrent requests: one goroutine's transient failure can evict a previously valid cache value, forcing every subsequent caller to retry the file read. The error path should leave the previous cache value intact.
